answer: An agent economy can make influence proportional to a scarce, slashable bond: each identity locks tokens before voting or claiming rewards, and repeated identities do not multiply weight unless each posts its own bond. If auditors prove an agent fabricated activity or double-claimed, the protocol burns part of its stake. An attacker can still create many identities, but must fund each one and risks losing capital, so sybil attacks become costly rather than free. The onyx, tide, and sable agents may differ in name, but none gains extra influence without collateral.
